The group came under particular scrutiny during pro-Palestine protests during the height of Israel’s genocide in Gaza and campus protests led by the student movement that started at Columbia University.

As settler violence against Palestinians intensifies during the annual olive harvest, Israeli authorities have stepped up measures against foreign activists, including bans and deportations.

The US has stepped up its efforts to choke Iran’s military supplies with the announcement of Task Force Iron Gate, a new unit aimed at blocking imports of weapons entering the Islamic Republic overland and via the Caspian Sea.
Washington and Tehran are locked in negotiations to end the current war, which has now lasted over eight months, crashed global markets, and has no clear end in sight.
While Iran produces the bulk of its weapons domestically, it has looked increasingly towards military imports from the north, amid the ongoing US naval blockade of its southern ports, which has brought its usual maritime trade routes to a near-standstill.
Arms and their components have entered Iran through Russia and Central Asia, while there is also growing evidence of sales from China.
Deliveries of the parts used in Iran’s home-produced missiles and drones have also been traced to manufacturers in countries opposed to the Islamic Republic, including the US itself.
Operational details are scarce about how the 20-person unit, inaugurated by US Admiral Brad Cooper of US Central Command in Tampa, Florida, will operate.
The task force also seeks to further block Iranian exports, the most lucrative being oil, which Washington has sanctioned and blockaded in its bid to curb what it calls Iran's "illegal revenue streams".

data.title: Middle East Eye: Britain sanctions Israeli settlement builders, Gaza aid-blocking activists
data.author: Katherine Hearst
data.summary:
Britain sanctions Israeli settlement builders, Gaza aid-blocking activists
The British government announced on Tuesday it would impose sanctions on eight Israeli construction companies involved in building settlements in the occupied West Bank and an activist group that prevents the delivery of aid to Gaza.
Britain announced asset freezes and director disqualifications on the eight companies including Har Hevron Development Company Ltd, Hemdat Shomron Ltd and S.A.G. (Velvel) Construction and Development Ltd, which construct and develop homes in the West Bank.
The government announced the sanctions package shortly before the final deadlines for the E1 tender, a settlement project which would bisect the Israeli-occupied West Bank and cut it off from East Jerusalem, fragmenting the land Palestinians hope will form the heart of a state.
"Protecting the two-state solution is the North Star of this Government's approach," the British foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, said in a statement. "That is why my message on E1 is clear: do not bid, do not build, and do not profit from the destruction of the two-state solution."
The government also imposed sanctions on Tzav 9, a group which it said had regularly blocked humanitarian aid trucks delivering food, water and fuel to the Gaza Strip.
Israel in September threatened to close the British Consulate building in East Jerusalem in response to London’s decision to impose trade sanctions on Israeli settlements in the West Bank.
British and Israeli diplomats last month reached a last-minute agreement to avoid the closure of the consulate.
Reporting by Reuters

The Foreign Office described Tsaz9 as "an Israeli activist movement whose stated mission has been to stop humanitarian aid entering the Gaza Strip, and which has organised and carried out blockades of crossings, ports and roads used by humanitarian aid convoys bound for Gaza".

Early last month, the chairman of Yemen’s Presidential Leadership Council, Rashad al-Alimi, announced the launch of Operation Fajr al-Yemen (Dawn of Yemen), aimed at restoring state institutions, retaking the capital, Sanaa, and ending Houthi control.
The announcement came a day after the Houthis, officially called Ansar Allah, seized large areas of Taiz governorate and took control of all entrances to Taiz city.
However, no advances have been made on the ground since the operation was announced. Instead, the Houthis have continued to make major gains in both Taiz and Lahij governorates, in Yemen's southwest.
On the west coast, battles were ongoing in Dhubab district, where government forces controlled the Dhubab military airport and surrounding areas. Meanwhile, the Houthis were advancing through the mountains and valleys of Lahij governorate and were on the verge of imposing a siege on military forces along the coast.
On Sunday, 15 November, Yemeni government forces announced the withdrawal of their troops from the Bab al-Mandab area and Dhubab military airport as part of a redeployment aimed at securing the provisional capital, Aden, and neighbouring governorates.
The Houthis advanced into all the areas previously held by government forces on the same day. They are now roughly 70km from Aden's northern entrance, while government forces are regrouping to defend the city.
